title: 'You Caused Oct 7': Nova Victim's Father Confronts Transportation Minister Regev at Likud Campaign Stop
detail: Nissim Louk — father of Shani Louk, the German-Israeli tattoo artist murdered at the Nova music festival on October 7, 2023 — confronted Transportation Minister Miri Regev outside Jerusalem's Mahane Yehuda market on Thursday, August 6, 2026, as she campaigned for the Likud party primaries. In video first reported by Ynet and shared widely on social media, Louk — wearing a t-shirt for the Orot HaShachar party — shouted 'You caused October 7! Shame on you all! Shame on Likud! My daughter Shani Louk was murdered because of you!' Likud activists at the scene challenged Louk, with one calling him 'trash' and others arguing opposition figures (Bennett, Liberman, Lapid) bore responsibility instead; Regev told him she was proud of Likud and noted her own daughter survived Nova. Regev's office said she 'spoke at length' with Louk, comforted him, and reiterated her commitment to a national commission investigating the events. In a companion interview published August 9, Louk described the moment on October 7 he first suspected his daughter was in danger — recognizing her small leg tattoos in a photo a friend sent around 10:00 a.m. before ZAKA volunteers later recovered her remains, confirmed by DNA — and renewed his call for accountability ahead of the October 27 election.

media.caption: Nissim Louk confronts Transportation Minister Miri Regev at a Likud campaign stop in Jerusalem
